editorial:
Imagine landing in a place where you feel like a stranger, only to find a friend who understands exactly what you are going through. You get to follow two young men, one from Somalia and one from Nigeria, who form a tight bond in a small part of Cardiff called Tiger Bay. The vibe is heavy but real, as you see them try to find their way while the neighborhood around them is being torn down and changed by rich developers. It is a story about loyalty and the struggle to keep your identity when the world wants to push you out.

What really hits home is the acting; the chemistry between the two leads feels like a real friendship, not a script. The pace is a bit slow at times, but it makes the emotional moments feel more honest. If you like stories about human connection and fighting for your home, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a bittersweet note as the neighborhood continues to change. After a series of fights and misunderstandings, the two friends realize that their bond is the only thing they truly own. They don't magically save the community from gentrification, but they find peace with each other. It wraps up by showing that even when you lose your home, the people you love become your real home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about immigrant life.
